posts.cooked:
Hi everyone,

I’m looking for an experienced automation developer who can help me build a video conferencing automation system using n8n + MirrorFly + API integrations.

This is a paid freelance project with clear requirements and a defined scope.

I’ll keep this as concise and technical as possible so you know exactly what’s involved.

Project Overview

I need to build an automated video conferencing workflow using n8n and MirrorFly that will:

  • Create video meetings automatically based on predefined triggers.

  • Generate meeting details and share them with participants.

  • Schedule meetings using calendar integrations.

  • Send meeting invitations and reminders through email or messaging services.

  • Manage meeting related events through webhooks and APIs.

  • (Optional add-on) Automate meeting recordings and post meeting notifications.

All of this needs to run through n8n workflows, with MirrorFly providing the video conferencing capabilities.

Core Requirements

1. MirrorFly Video Conferencing Integration

  • Integrate MirrorFly Video Call API and SDK.

  • Create and manage video meetings through supported APIs.

  • Generate or retrieve meeting joining details.

  • Handle meeting events through webhooks or callbacks where supported.

  • Support one to one and group video calls.

  • Connect MirrorFly with n8n using HTTP requests, webhooks, or a custom integration where required.

2. Meeting Scheduling and Management

  • Trigger meeting creation from form submissions, CRM updates, or other events.

  • Integrate with Google Calendar, Calendly, or similar scheduling services.

  • Send meeting invitations to participants.

  • Schedule automatic reminders before meetings.

  • Handle meeting cancellations and rescheduling.

3. Automated Notifications

  • Send meeting details through email or supported messaging services.

  • Notify participants when a meeting is scheduled, updated, or cancelled.

  • Send reminders at predefined intervals.

  • Support optional Slack or Microsoft Teams notifications.

  • Use structured data to pass meeting details between workflows.

4. CRM Integration

Integrate with HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive to:

  • Trigger meeting workflows based on CRM events.

  • Associate meetings with relevant contacts or deals.

  • Update CRM records when meetings are scheduled or completed.

  • Store meeting details and supported recording links.

5. Post Meeting Automation

  • Trigger workflows when a meeting ends, using supported events or callbacks.

  • Send follow up emails to participants.

  • Update CRM records with meeting status.

  • Store meeting metadata and recording links when available.

  • Trigger additional workflows based on meeting outcomes.

6. Optional Premium Feature: Meeting Recording and Streaming

If you have experience with video recording and streaming integrations, please mention it.

This feature may include:

  • Automating meeting recording through supported MirrorFly capabilities.

  • Retrieving recording details or links.

  • Triggering workflows when recordings become available.

  • Integrating supported RTMP or HLS streaming workflows where required.

Tech Stack

You must be comfortable with:

  • n8n: Webhooks, HTTP Request nodes, conditional logic, API integrations, and asynchronous workflows.

  • MirrorFly: Video Call API, SDK integration, and supported meeting capabilities.

  • Calendar APIs: Google Calendar, Calendly, or similar services.

  • CRM integrations: HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive.

  • Backend development: JavaScript or other technologies when a custom integration is required.

Deliverables

  • Fully configured n8n workflows.

  • MirrorFly integration with the required video conferencing functionality.

  • Automated meeting scheduling and notification workflows.

  • Documentation for future maintenance.

  • One handover and training session.

  • 30 days of bug support after delivery.

Budget

The budget is flexible depending on experience, but roughly:

  • Base system: £800–£1,000

  • Advanced features and integrations: £800–£1,200

Payment can be arranged through an agreed platform.

How to Apply

Please reply with:

  • Your experience with n8n and API integrations.

  • Your experience integrating video conferencing APIs or SDKs, preferably MirrorFly.

  • Examples of similar automation projects.

  • Your availability.

  • Estimated delivery timeline.

  • Your pricing for the base system.

  • Your pricing for advanced features and integrations.

I’m ready to start immediately with the right developer.

Thanks!

posts.name: Matt Michels
posts.cooked:
I’m building this kind of automation for my own business, so the n8n scheduling, reminder and CRM flow you describe is familiar ground.

  1. I build n8n workflows on a self-hosted instance, always with signature-verified webhooks and error branches. My n8n work so far is test-built on localhost, not client production. Most production integrations of mine run as Supabase edge functions and Python workers.

  2. I haven’t integrated MirrorFly or any video conferencing SDK. Closest analog: Twilio voice webhooks and Vapi voice agents, where I handle call events and callbacks. I’d read the MirrorFly API docs first.

  3. Missed-call text-back: a signed Twilio webhook triggers a text to the caller, logs the miss to Postgres and pushes the contact into HubSpot. Also an n8n flow that upserts a HubSpot contact and deal from a webhook without duplicates. Both could feed your meeting triggers and CRM updates.

  4. About 20 hours a week, US Eastern time (Detroit).

  5. I’d rather scope it after reading the MirrorFly docs than guess a number now. I’d give you a milestone breakdown with dates once the API surface is clear.

  6. I’d quote a fixed price for the base system after that scoping step. I won’t give you a number I can’t stand behind.

  7. Advanced features, such as the recording and streaming add-on, would get their own fixed quote after scoping. I haven’t built recording or RTMP/HLS workflows, so I’d verify what MirrorFly supports first.

I can walk you through the HubSpot and missed-call builds on a live screen-share, and you can reply here or DM.

Video APIs. Built against Twilio for voice and messaging, and worked with RTMP streaming. Not MirrorFly specifically, and I would rather say so than claim otherwise. I would spend day one in their docs and a sandbox before committing to a fixed timeline.

One flag worth raising now. MirrorFly is SDK-first, built for embedding into your own app rather than generating hosted meeting links the way Zoom does. Your brief assumes an API call returns a joining link you can email out. Depending on your plan and whether you have a host application, that may need a small frontend for people to actually join. Disclosure: I’m affiliated with Pond AI.

Hi Shyam, your scope is clear, and I’ve mapped it into a diagram (attached). It follows your brief in three stages:

Trigger + schedule: a form, CRM event or Calendly booking creates the MirrorFly meeting and the Google Calendar event together.

  1. Meeting + notify: n8n handles webhooks, retries and dedupe, then sends invites, reminders and change notices by email, with optional Slack or Teams alerts.
  2. After the call: MirrorFly’s call-ended callback sends status and any recording link to the CRM, linked to the right deal, then a follow-up email goes out.

Reminders come from one meeting record per room (status, UTC start time, time zones), so a reschedule or cancel never leaves a stale reminder. Failures route to a human instead of silently dropping a meeting.

Neither is video conferencing, but both are multi-step, CRM-connected automations that went live fast.
  • Availability: The team and the dev are ready to start now.

Where Pond AI fits: you get a team that treats this as a production system, with error handling, alerts, human handoff, docs, your handover session and 30 days of bug support. Meetings run end to end from one trigger, every call is logged against the right deal, and you don’t depend on one freelancer’s memory of how it works. You also pay for results, not attempts.

Long Wait nodes are hard to cancel when a meeting moves. Instead of waiting inside the workflow, keep one record per MirrorFly room (status, start time in UTC, participant time zones). Also pick one source of truth for the meeting time (the calendar or the CRM) and tag every record the workflow writes. That stops a CRM update from n8n creating a second meeting and looping.

For the recording add-on, if participants are in the UK or EU, put a recording notice in the invite and decide how long the links stay on the CRM record.

That keeps the meetings, invites, and follow-ups in one loop without silent drops.

Good day @Shyamvijay your project bridges asynchronous webhook event with deterministic scheduling, which introduces three specific architectural risk that most developers hit until they hit production.

First, relying on long static wait nodes for meeting reminder will inevitably fail when an event is rescheduled. The correct pattern is to maintain a single master database record for each meeting room tracking UTC start time, active time zone and current status. A scheduled n8n worker then polls this record on a rolling 15 minutes window to trigger reminder dynamically. This eliminates stale notification entirely.

Second risk is syncing both Google Calendar and a CRM. This creates bidirectional write conflict. One system should be designated as the strict source of truth, typically the calendar of event scheduling and the CRM for deal tracking. Any writes to the secondary system must be tagged with a metadata flag so n8n can filter them out during webhook processing. Without this tag, infinite sync loops that breaks the workflow logic will be generated.

Third risk, handling post meeting recordings requires careful compliance framing before any API calls reach your CRM. UK and EU recording regulations mandate explicit consent notices and defined retention windows. Your n8n workflow should capture the recording link, verify that consent flag is active and only then route the media metadata to Salesforce, HubSpot or Pipedrive. This protects you from automatic compliance violation while keeping the data pipeline fully automated.

One thing decides how this is built: MirrorFly creates meeting links in its SDK, not its REST API, so the video side needs a small page next to n8n.   • Every trigger carries an ID, so a repeated webhook never creates a second meeting or a duplicate CRM entry.
  • Reminders are skipped automatically when a meeting is moved or cancelled, and times are sent in each participant’s own time zone.
  • If a step fails, you get an alert straight away, so a meeting never disappears silently.

posts.name: MG DIGITAL AGENCY
posts.cooked:
n8n + MirrorFly Video Conferencing Automation

A reliable video conferencing automation system needs to do more than generate meeting links. It must keep scheduling, notifications, and CRM records synchronized throughout the entire meeting lifecycle—including rescheduling, cancellations, unexpected API responses, and webhook retries.

Our approach is to build a structured, dependable automation system where each workflow has a clear purpose, predictable behavior, and a defined way to handle failures and recovery.

1. Core Automation System

The implementation will cover:

  • MirrorFly integration: Create and manage 1:1 and group meetings, handle meeting details, and connect supported API events to n8n.
  • Scheduling automation: Trigger meetings from an agreed source and manage scheduling, rescheduling, and cancellations.
  • Calendar integration: Coordinate meeting schedules, invitations, and reminders through one calendar provider.
  • CRM synchronization: Connect one CRM, associate meetings with relevant contacts or deals, and update meeting status and details.
  • Notifications: Send automated email notifications for meeting confirmations, changes, reminders, and other agreed events.
  • Workflow reliability: Implement duplicate-event prevention, retry handling, conditional routing, and error logging to make the automation more resilient.

2. Implementation and Quality Assurance

The workflow design will account for the complete meeting lifecycle, rather than treating each integration as an isolated task.

The implementation process includes:

  • Defining integration boundaries, data mapping, and expected event behavior.
  • Configuring and validating API and webhook connections.
  • Testing successful operations as well as cancellations, repeated events, synchronization failures, and recovery scenarios.
  • Delivering organized, exportable n8n workflows with documentation and a handover session.

Estimated delivery: 12 working days, assuming timely access to the required systems and no substantial changes to the agreed scope.

3. Advanced Automation

The advanced phase can extend the core system with supported recording workflows, recording-availability notifications, recording metadata and links, automated post-meeting follow-ups, and additional CRM updates.

RTMP/HLS streaming, additional service providers, or a new calling interface will depend on the available integration capabilities and may require separate scoping.

The current scope assumes that an existing web or mobile application can host the MirrorFly SDK. Building a new calling interface or embedding the SDK into a new application would need to be agreed separately.

Estimated additional delivery: 8 working days, subject to technical validation of the required capabilities.

4. Post-Delivery Support

The project includes 30 calendar days of bug support, starting after final delivery and client acceptance.

  • Reproducible defects within the agreed scope will be corrected without additional development charges.
  • Standard issues will receive an initial response within one business day.
  • Critical issues will receive an initial response within four business hours during business hours.
  • These are initial-response targets, not guaranteed resolution times.

New features, scope changes, additional integrations, third-party outages, and breaking changes introduced by external providers are outside the included support.

5. Commercial Overview

The base implementation is £1,000, with an estimated delivery period of 12 working days. The advanced phase is an additional £1,200, with an estimated 8 further working days. The phases can be commissioned together or agreed separately.

The final scope, acceptance criteria, and payment terms can be agreed mutually through the chosen platform before work begins.

The goal is to deliver a maintainable automation system that connects meetings, scheduling, communications, and CRM operations into one coherent process—with clear workflows, reliable event handling, and documentation that makes future maintenance easier.

One Quick Question Before We Finalize the Scope

For the MirrorFly calling interface, which situation applies to your project?

A) The existing web/mobile app already has the MirrorFly SDK, so the focus is on n8n automation and integrations.

B) The calling interface or SDK integration also needs to be built.

A or B is enough. This will help establish the right integration scope and delivery plan from the outset.

Hi Shayam, two things I’d decide before building anything. First pick one source of truth for the meeting time, either the celendar or the CRM. if n8n updates a CRM deal and that update triggers the ‘‘create meeting’’ workflow again, you get duplicate meetings. A simple fix is to tag every record n8n writes (a field like updated_by = n8n ) and have the trigger ignore those.

Second, for reminders and reschedules, I’d keep one record per meeting with the status, the start time in UTC and each participants’s time zone, and run a scheduled workflow that sends whatever reminders are due. A reschedule or cancel then just updates the record. Long Wait nodes are hard to cancel once a meeting moves.

If you add recording and participants are in the UK or EU, put a recording links are kept before you store them in the CRM. That’s easier to set up now than to fix later.

I’m with Pond Ai, where we build custom AI agents around existing stacks like n8n. We usually start by mapping the architecture for the whole flow, and that part is free, so you can keep it even if someone else builds it.

posts.name: Abdullah Nadeem
posts.cooked:
Hi @Shyamvijay,

A few of the replies here have already flagged the MirrorFly architecture question, and they’re right to. MirrorFly generates meeting links through its client SDK (createMeetLink), not through a REST API endpoint. That means n8n can’t call an HTTP endpoint and get a join URL back the way it would with Zoom or Google Meet. The workflow needs a small Node.js bridge service sitting between n8n and MirrorFly that handles the SDK call and returns the meeting details to n8n via webhook. Without that bridge, the entire meeting creation step breaks.

That said, once the bridge is in place, the rest of this project is standard n8n territory, and it’s exactly the kind of system I build daily.

On the scheduling and notification layer, I’ve built production systems in n8n that handle the full meeting lifecycle: creation from triggers (form submissions, CRM events, webhook callbacks), calendar integration via Cal.com and Google Calendar, automated invitations, pre-meeting reminders, and cancellation/rescheduling logic. One of my production systems is an AI voice receptionist that handles inbound calls, books appointments via Cal.com, recognizes returning callers, and manages rescheduling and cancellations with zero human involvement.
Case study: AI Voice Receptionist: Zero-Wait Appointment Scheduling via Cal.com | Case Study

On CRM integration, I’ve built systems across HubSpot, GoHighLevel, Close CRM, and Airtable. My RevOps architecture for a SaaS company spans 4 platforms (GoHighLevel, Close CRM, Airtable, n8n) with deterministic attribution, duplicate-safe lead ingestion, and post-sale payment automation, all event-driven through n8n.
Case study: Kronk AI: Revenue Operations Architecture — GHL + Close CRM + Airtable + n8n | Case Study

On webhook and callback handling, every workflow I ship uses production-grade error handling: try/catch patterns, retry logic with configurable backoff, idempotent deduplication (so a repeated webhook never creates a duplicate meeting or CRM record), and error workflows that send alerts the moment something fails. I’ve built webhook-driven systems for Retell AI voice agents, Twilio SMS/voice, and multi-step API chains where the callback architecture is identical to what MirrorFly uses.

On the reminder problem that a few replies mentioned: I agree that Long Wait nodes are the wrong approach for meetings that can be rescheduled. I’d use a meeting record table (room ID, status, UTC start time, participant time zones) and a scheduled n8n sub-workflow that checks for upcoming meetings due for a reminder. If someone reschedules or cancels, updating that one record kills the old reminder instantly. No orphaned wait branches.

On post-meeting automation, I build follow-up workflows as a standard part of every CRM integration I deliver. Post-call transcript analysis, status updates, follow-up email triggers, and recording link storage are all patterns I’ve shipped in production.

One question before scoping: do you already have an application where participants join the MirrorFly calls, or would the developer also need to build that participant-facing interface? That’s the single biggest variable in the project scope.

loaded_posts.cooked:
Hi everyone,

I’m looking for an experienced automation developer who can help me build a video conferencing automation system using n8n + MirrorFly + API integrations.

This is a paid freelance project with clear requirements and a defined scope.

I’ll keep this as concise and technical as possible so you know exactly what’s involved.

Project Overview

I need to build an automated video conferencing workflow using n8n and MirrorFly that will:

  • Create video meetings automatically based on predefined triggers.

  • Generate meeting details and share them with participants.

  • Schedule meetings using calendar integrations.

  • Send meeting invitations and reminders through email or messaging services.

  • Manage meeting related events through webhooks and APIs.

  • (Optional add-on) Automate meeting recordings and post meeting notifications.

All of this needs to run through n8n workflows, with MirrorFly providing the video conferencing capabilities.

Core Requirements

1. MirrorFly Video Conferencing Integration

  • Integrate MirrorFly Video Call API and SDK.

  • Create and manage video meetings through supported APIs.

  • Generate or retrieve meeting joining details.

  • Handle meeting events through webhooks or callbacks where supported.

  • Support one to one and group video calls.

  • Connect MirrorFly with n8n using HTTP requests, webhooks, or a custom integration where required.

2. Meeting Scheduling and Management

  • Trigger meeting creation from form submissions, CRM updates, or other events.

  • Integrate with Google Calendar, Calendly, or similar scheduling services.

  • Send meeting invitations to participants.

  • Schedule automatic reminders before meetings.

  • Handle meeting cancellations and rescheduling.

3. Automated Notifications

  • Send meeting details through email or supported messaging services.

  • Notify participants when a meeting is scheduled, updated, or cancelled.

  • Send reminders at predefined intervals.

  • Support optional Slack or Microsoft Teams notifications.

  • Use structured data to pass meeting details between workflows.

4. CRM Integration

Integrate with HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive to:

  • Trigger meeting workflows based on CRM events.

  • Associate meetings with relevant contacts or deals.

  • Update CRM records when meetings are scheduled or completed.

  • Store meeting details and supported recording links.

5. Post Meeting Automation

  • Trigger workflows when a meeting ends, using supported events or callbacks.

  • Send follow up emails to participants.

  • Update CRM records with meeting status.

  • Store meeting metadata and recording links when available.

  • Trigger additional workflows based on meeting outcomes.

6. Optional Premium Feature: Meeting Recording and Streaming

If you have experience with video recording and streaming integrations, please mention it.

This feature may include:

  • Automating meeting recording through supported MirrorFly capabilities.

  • Retrieving recording details or links.

  • Triggering workflows when recordings become available.

  • Integrating supported RTMP or HLS streaming workflows where required.

Tech Stack

You must be comfortable with:

  • n8n: Webhooks, HTTP Request nodes, conditional logic, API integrations, and asynchronous workflows.

  • MirrorFly: Video Call API, SDK integration, and supported meeting capabilities.

  • Calendar APIs: Google Calendar, Calendly, or similar services.

  • CRM integrations: HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive.

  • Backend development: JavaScript or other technologies when a custom integration is required.

Deliverables

  • Fully configured n8n workflows.

  • MirrorFly integration with the required video conferencing functionality.

  • Automated meeting scheduling and notification workflows.

  • Documentation for future maintenance.

  • One handover and training session.

  • 30 days of bug support after delivery.

Budget

The budget is flexible depending on experience, but roughly:

  • Base system: £800–£1,000

  • Advanced features and integrations: £800–£1,200

Payment can be arranged through an agreed platform.

How to Apply

Please reply with:

  • Your experience with n8n and API integrations.

  • Your experience integrating video conferencing APIs or SDKs, preferably MirrorFly.

  • Examples of similar automation projects.

  • Your availability.

  • Estimated delivery timeline.

  • Your pricing for the base system.

  • Your pricing for advanced features and integrations.

I’m ready to start immediately with the right developer.

Thanks!

Long Wait nodes are hard to cancel when a meeting moves. Instead of waiting inside the workflow, keep one record per MirrorFly room (status, start time in UTC, participant time zones). Good day @Shyamvijay your project bridges asynchronous webhook event with deterministic scheduling, which introduces three specific architectural risk that most developers hit until they hit production.

First, relying on long static wait nodes for meeting reminder will inevitably fail when an event is rescheduled. The correct pattern is to maintain a single master database record for each meeting room tracking UTC start time, active time zone and current status. A scheduled n8n worker then polls this record on a rolling 15 minutes window to trigger reminder dynamically. This eliminates stale notification entirely.

Second risk is syncing both Google Calendar and a CRM. This creates bidirectional write conflict. One system should be designated as the strict source of truth, typically the calendar of event scheduling and the CRM for deal tracking. Any writes to the secondary system must be tagged with a metadata flag so n8n can filter them out during webhook processing. Without this tag, infinite sync loops that breaks the workflow logic will be generated.

Third risk, handling post meeting recordings requires careful compliance framing before any API calls reach your CRM. UK and EU recording regulations mandate explicit consent notices and defined retention windows. Your n8n workflow should capture the recording link, verify that consent flag is active and only then route the media metadata to Salesforce, HubSpot or Pipedrive. This protects you from automatic compliance violation while keeping the data pipeline fully automated.

Hi Shyam,

One thing decides how this is built: MirrorFly creates meeting links in its SDK, not its REST API, so the video side needs a small page next to n8n. That’s the part I’ve actually built before: a video-meeting app with scheduled and instant calls, guest join links, recordings, transcripts and AI summaries, driven by call webhooks (started, ended, recording ready). So the video side won’t be new ground for me.

How I’d build it

  • A small join page creates the MirrorFly room and gives n8n the link in one call. Everything else stays in n8n, where you can see and change it.
  • Join links are protected, so only invited people get in and an old link can’t be reused.
  • Every trigger carries an ID, so a repeated webhook never creates a second meeting or a duplicate CRM entry.
  • Reminders are skipped automatically when a meeting is moved or cancelled, and times are sent in each participant’s own time zone.
  • If a step fails, you get an alert straight away, so a meeting never disappears silently.

Your questions

  1. n8n and APIs: webhooks, HTTP Request nodes, retries and error branches, Google Calendar and Calendly, email and Slack/Teams notifications, HubSpot/Pipedrive/Salesforce updates.
  2. Video SDKs: I’ve built a full video-meeting app with a commercial video SDK and its webhooks. I haven’t used MirrorFly itself, so I check your licence on day one before building anything else.
  3. Similar work: the video app above, plus a live production web app that sends automated email and push notifications on every status change.
  4. Availability: I can start now, full-time on this.
  5. Timeline: in 2 days you see a real meeting link created on your MirrorFly licence and pushed through n8n. The base system takes 10 to 12 days, and the advanced features about 7 more.
  6. Base system: £700. That covers meeting creation, the join page, calendar, invites, reminders, reschedule and cancel, full written documentation, a recorded handover and 30 days of bug support.
  7. Advanced features: £850 for the CRM sync, post-meeting follow-ups (with a separate path for no-shows), recording links and Slack/Teams alerts.

You pay by milestone, and each milestone ends with a short screen recording of it working, so you only pay for what you’ve seen.

I work in writing: you get a short written plan before I start and clear documentation at every step, so you always know what is built and how to change it.

Hi Shayam, two things I’d decide before building anything. First pick one source of truth for the meeting time, either the celendar or the CRM. if n8n updates a CRM deal and that update triggers the ‘‘create meeting’’ workflow again, you get duplicate meetings. A simple fix is to tag every record n8n writes (a field like updated_by = n8n ) and have the trigger ignore those.

Second, for reminders and reschedules, I’d keep one record per meeting with the status, the start time in UTC and each participants’s time zone, and run a scheduled workflow that sends whatever reminders are due. A reschedule or cancel then just updates the record. Long Wait nodes are hard to cancel once a meeting moves.

If you add recording and participants are in the UK or EU, put a recording links are kept before you store them in the CRM. That’s easier to set up now than to fix later.

I’m with Pond Ai, where we build custom AI agents around existing stacks like n8n. We usually start by mapping the architecture for the whole flow, and that part is free, so you can keep it even if someone else builds it.

loaded_posts.cooked:
Hi @Shyamvijay,

A few of the replies here have already flagged the MirrorFly architecture question, and they’re right to. MirrorFly generates meeting links through its client SDK (createMeetLink), not through a REST API endpoint. That means n8n can’t call an HTTP endpoint and get a join URL back the way it would with Zoom or Google Meet. The workflow needs a small Node.js bridge service sitting between n8n and MirrorFly that handles the SDK call and returns the meeting details to n8n via webhook. Without that bridge, the entire meeting creation step breaks.

That said, once the bridge is in place, the rest of this project is standard n8n territory, and it’s exactly the kind of system I build daily.

On the scheduling and notification layer, I’ve built production systems in n8n that handle the full meeting lifecycle: creation from triggers (form submissions, CRM events, webhook callbacks), calendar integration via Cal.com and Google Calendar, automated invitations, pre-meeting reminders, and cancellation/rescheduling logic. One of my production systems is an AI voice receptionist that handles inbound calls, books appointments via Cal.com, recognizes returning callers, and manages rescheduling and cancellations with zero human involvement.
Case study: AI Voice Receptionist: Zero-Wait Appointment Scheduling via Cal.com | Case Study

On CRM integration, I’ve built systems across HubSpot, GoHighLevel, Close CRM, and Airtable. My RevOps architecture for a SaaS company spans 4 platforms (GoHighLevel, Close CRM, Airtable, n8n) with deterministic attribution, duplicate-safe lead ingestion, and post-sale payment automation, all event-driven through n8n.
Case study: Kronk AI: Revenue Operations Architecture — GHL + Close CRM + Airtable + n8n | Case Study

On webhook and callback handling, every workflow I ship uses production-grade error handling: try/catch patterns, retry logic with configurable backoff, idempotent deduplication (so a repeated webhook never creates a duplicate meeting or CRM record), and error workflows that send alerts the moment something fails. I’ve built webhook-driven systems for Retell AI voice agents, Twilio SMS/voice, and multi-step API chains where the callback architecture is identical to what MirrorFly uses.

On the reminder problem that a few replies mentioned: I agree that Long Wait nodes are the wrong approach for meetings that can be rescheduled. I’d use a meeting record table (room ID, status, UTC start time, participant time zones) and a scheduled n8n sub-workflow that checks for upcoming meetings due for a reminder. If someone reschedules or cancels, updating that one record kills the old reminder instantly. No orphaned wait branches.

On post-meeting automation, I build follow-up workflows as a standard part of every CRM integration I deliver. Post-call transcript analysis, status updates, follow-up email triggers, and recording link storage are all patterns I’ve shipped in production.

One question before scoping: do you already have an application where participants join the MirrorFly calls, or would the developer also need to build that participant-facing interface? That’s the single biggest variable in the project scope.

@Shyamvijay  Hello, I hope you see this. I looked at the reminder and reschedule part, because that is where these meeting flows usually break. 
 Long Wait nodes are hard to cancel when a meeting moves. Instead of waiting inside the workflow, keep one record per MirrorFly room (status, start time in UTC, participant time zones). A scheduled n8n run checks that record and sends only the reminders that are due. If someone reschedules or cancels, you just update the row. Old reminders never go out. 
 Also pick one source of truth for the meeting time (the calendar or the CRM) and tag every record the workflow writes. That stops a CRM update from n8n creating a second meeting and looping. 
 For the recording add-on, if participants are in the UK or EU, put a recording notice in the invite and decide how long the links stay on the CRM record. 
 That keeps the meetings, invites, and follow-ups in one loop without silent drops.

comments.author: Odoemelamair
comments.text:
Good day  @Shyamvijay  your project bridges asynchronous webhook event with deterministic scheduling, which introduces three specific architectural risk that most developers hit until they hit production. 
 First, relying on long static wait nodes for meeting reminder will inevitably fail when an event is rescheduled. The correct pattern is to maintain a single master database record for each meeting room tracking UTC start time, active time zone and current status. A scheduled n8n worker then polls this record on a rolling 15 minutes window to trigger reminder dynamically.  This eliminates stale notification entirely. 
 Second risk is syncing both Google Calendar and a CRM. This creates bidirectional write conflict. One system should be designated as the strict source of truth, typically the calendar of event scheduling and the CRM for deal tracking. Any writes to the secondary system must be tagged with a metadata flag so n8n can filter them out during webhook processing. Without this tag, infinite sync loops that breaks the workflow logic will be generated. 
 Third risk, handling post meeting recordings requires careful compliance framing before any API calls reach your CRM. UK and EU recording regulations mandate explicit consent notices and defined retention windows. Your n8n workflow should capture the recording link, verify that consent flag is active and only then route the media metadata to Salesforce, HubSpot or Pipedrive. This protects you from automatic compliance violation while keeping the data pipeline fully automated. 
 I am affiliated with Pond AI, we build production grade n8n workflow with robust error routing and video SDK lifecycle management. We are available to start immediately, with delivery timeline and pricing tailored directly to your exact scope following a quick architecture review. 
 We provide a free architecture map outlining your workflow design that is yours to keep, even if you build in-house or hire another developer. Should you choose to build with  Pond AI , your project includes a risk free 7-days money-back guarantee if agreed.

Hi Shyam, one thing that usually causes problems on these meeting setups is when a reschedule happens after reminders have already been queued. 
 Instead of using long Wait nodes, store one row per MirrorFly room with the status, start time in UTC, and the time zones of the people joining. Then run a short scheduled workflow that looks at that row and sends only the reminders that are actually due. A cancel or time change just updates the same row, so nothing old gets sent. 
 Also decide early whether the calendar or the CRM owns the meeting time, and mark every record the workflow writes. That stops an update from n8n creating a second meeting by mistake. 
 If you add recording later and any participants are in the UK or EU, include a short recording notice in the invite and set how long those links stay on the CRM record. 
 That covers the create, notify, change, and log steps without the usual silent failures.

n8n + MirrorFly Video Conferencing Automation 
 A reliable video conferencing automation system needs to do more than generate meeting links. It must keep scheduling, notifications, and CRM records synchronized throughout the entire meeting lifecycle—including rescheduling, cancellations, unexpected API responses, and webhook retries. 
 Our approach is to build a structured, dependable automation system where each workflow has a clear purpose, predictable behavior, and a defined way to handle failures and recovery. 
   1. Core Automation System 
 The implementation will cover: 
 
  MirrorFly integration:  Create and manage 1:1 and group meetings, handle meeting details, and connect supported API events to n8n. 
  Scheduling automation:  Trigger meetings from an agreed source and manage scheduling, rescheduling, and cancellations. 
  Calendar integration:  Coordinate meeting schedules, invitations, and reminders through one calendar provider. 
  CRM synchronization:  Connect one CRM, associate meetings with relevant contacts or deals, and update meeting status and details. 
  Notifications:  Send automated email notifications for meeting confirmations, changes, reminders, and other agreed events. 
  Workflow reliability:  Implement duplicate-event prevention, retry handling, conditional routing, and error logging to make the automation more resilient. 
 
   2. Implementation and Quality Assurance 
 The workflow design will account for the complete meeting lifecycle, rather than treating each integration as an isolated task. 
 The implementation process includes: 
 
 Defining integration boundaries, data mapping, and expected event behavior. 
 Configuring and validating API and webhook connections. 
 Testing successful operations as well as cancellations, repeated events, synchronization failures, and recovery scenarios. 
 Delivering organized, exportable n8n workflows with documentation and a handover session. 
 
  Estimated delivery:  12 working days, assuming timely access to the required systems and no substantial changes to the agreed scope. 
   3. Advanced Automation 
 The advanced phase can extend the core system with supported recording workflows, recording-availability notifications, recording metadata and links, automated post-meeting follow-ups, and additional CRM updates. 
 RTMP/HLS streaming, additional service providers, or a new calling interface will depend on the available integration capabilities and may require separate scoping. 
 The current scope assumes that an existing web or mobile application can host the MirrorFly SDK. Building a new calling interface or embedding the SDK into a new application would need to be agreed separately. 
  Estimated additional delivery:  8 working days, subject to technical validation of the required capabilities. 
   4. Post-Delivery Support 
 The project includes  30 calendar days of bug support , starting after final delivery and client acceptance. 
 
 Reproducible defects within the agreed scope will be corrected without additional development charges. 
 Standard issues will receive an initial response within one business day. 
 Critical issues will receive an initial response within four business hours during business hours. 
 These are initial-response targets, not guaranteed resolution times. 
 
 New features, scope changes, additional integrations, third-party outages, and breaking changes introduced by external providers are outside the included support. 
   5. Commercial Overview 
 The base implementation is  £1,000 , with an estimated delivery period of 12 working days. The advanced phase is an additional  £1,200 , with an estimated 8 further working days. The phases can be commissioned together or agreed separately. 
 The final scope, acceptance criteria, and payment terms can be agreed mutually through the chosen platform before work begins. 
 The goal is to deliver a maintainable automation system that connects meetings, scheduling, communications, and CRM operations into one coherent process—with clear workflows, reliable event handling, and documentation that makes future maintenance easier.

comments.author: CallmeSaad
comments.text:
Hi Shayam, two things I’d decide before building anything. First pick one source of truth for the meeting time, either the celendar or the CRM. if n8n updates a CRM deal and that update triggers the ‘‘create meeting’’ workflow again, you get duplicate meetings. A simple fix is to tag every record n8n writes (a field like  updated_by  =  n8n ) and have the trigger ignore those. 
 Second, for reminders and reschedules, I’d keep one record per meeting with the status, the start time in UTC and each participants’s time zone, and run a scheduled workflow that sends whatever reminders are due. A reschedule or cancel then just updates the record. Long Wait nodes are hard to cancel once a meeting moves. 
 If you add recording and participants are in the UK or EU, put a recording links are kept before you store them in the CRM. That’s easier to set up now than to fix later. 
 I’m with Pond Ai, where we build custom AI agents around existing stacks like n8n. We usually start by mapping the architecture for the whole flow, and that part is free, so you can keep it even if someone else builds it.

comments.author: abdullah30
comments.text:
Hi  @Shyamvijay , 
 A few of the replies here have already flagged the MirrorFly architecture question, and they’re right to. MirrorFly generates meeting links through its client SDK (createMeetLink), not through a REST API endpoint. That means n8n can’t call an HTTP endpoint and get a join URL back the way it would with Zoom or Google Meet. The workflow needs a small Node.js bridge service sitting between n8n and MirrorFly that handles the SDK call and returns the meeting details to n8n via webhook. Without that bridge, the entire meeting creation step breaks. 
 That said, once the bridge is in place, the rest of this project is standard n8n territory, and it’s exactly the kind of system I build daily. 
  On the scheduling and notification layer , I’ve built production systems in n8n that handle the full meeting lifecycle: creation from triggers (form submissions, CRM events, webhook callbacks), calendar integration via  Cal.com  and Google Calendar, automated invitations, pre-meeting reminders, and cancellation/rescheduling logic. One of my production systems is an AI voice receptionist that handles inbound calls, books appointments via  Cal.com , recognizes returning callers, and manages rescheduling and cancellations with zero human involvement. 
Case study:  AI Voice Receptionist: Zero-Wait Appointment Scheduling via Cal.com | Case Study  
  On CRM integration , I’ve built systems across HubSpot, GoHighLevel, Close CRM, and Airtable. My RevOps architecture for a SaaS company spans 4 platforms (GoHighLevel, Close CRM, Airtable, n8n) with deterministic attribution, duplicate-safe lead ingestion, and post-sale payment automation, all event-driven through n8n. 
Case study:  Kronk AI: Revenue Operations Architecture — GHL + Close CRM + Airtable + n8n | Case Study  
  On webhook and callback handling , every workflow I ship uses production-grade error handling: try/catch patterns, retry logic with configurable backoff, idempotent deduplication (so a repeated webhook never creates a duplicate meeting or CRM record), and error workflows that send alerts the moment something fails. I’ve built webhook-driven systems for Retell AI voice agents, Twilio SMS/voice, and multi-step API chains where the callback architecture is identical to what MirrorFly uses. 
  On the reminder problem  that a few replies mentioned: I agree that Long Wait nodes are the wrong approach for meetings that can be rescheduled. I’d use a meeting record table (room ID, status, UTC start time, participant time zones) and a scheduled n8n sub-workflow that checks for upcoming meetings due for a reminder. If someone reschedules or cancels, updating that one record kills the old reminder instantly. No orphaned wait branches. 
  On post-meeting automation , I build follow-up workflows as a standard part of every CRM integration I deliver. Post-call transcript analysis, status updates, follow-up email triggers, and recording link storage are all patterns I’ve shipped in production. 
 One question before scoping: do you already have an application where participants join the MirrorFly calls, or would the developer also need to build that participant-facing interface? That’s the single biggest variable in the project scope.
